summary: Iteration 6 production hardening pass — 18/18 new iteration-6 tests PASS, 27/27 prior iteration-4 auth regression tests PASS. Verified Fernet encryption at rest (DB values prefixed 'enc::v1::'), API redaction of ssh.password/private_key and smtp_password, masked-roundtrip preservation, /api/health (no DB) and /api/ready (DB ping), MongoDB indexes (servers.id unique + vendor, checkouts.server_id, reservations.server_id, alert_events.timestamp DESC, audit TTL on 'ts'), audit log query excludes internal 'ts' field, auto-sync loop started (log line confirmed in backend stderr). One real production-hardening bug found: _set_auth_cookies() hardcodes secure=False so COOKIE_SECURE env is honored ONLY by /auth/refresh — login/setup cookies will never get the Secure flag even when COOKIE_SECURE=true.

critical.issue: _set_auth_cookies() (server.py:813-816) hardcodes secure=False. It ignores the COOKIE_SECURE env var entirely. Only the /auth/refresh endpoint (server.py:972-974) reads COOKIE_SECURE. Verified live: curl POST /api/auth/login returns Set-Cookie for access_token and refresh_token WITHOUT the Secure flag (HttpOnly + SameSite=lax only). This defeats the whole point of the COOKIE_SECURE iteration-6 feature on HTTPS deployments — initial login cookies remain non-Secure.

minor.issue: Query uses projection {'_id': 0, 'ts': 0} but does not exclude potentially leaked future internal fields. Currently safe — 'ts' is hidden correctly. No action needed.

db.audit.drop_indexes() is called unconditionally on every startup before recreating indexes. This works but slightly impacts cold-start; consider only recreating the TTL index when AUDIT_TTL_DAYS changes.

action_items:
FIX (HIGH): Update _set_auth_cookies() at server.py:813-816 to read COOKIE_SECURE env var (same pattern as /auth/refresh line 972). Currently the common dict hardcodes secure=False — this nullifies COOKIE_SECURE for login/setup endpoints. Suggested fix:
```
def _set_auth_cookies(response: Response, access: str, refresh: str):
    secure = os.environ.get('COOKIE_SECURE', 'false').lower() in ('1','true','yes')
    common = dict(httponly=True, samesite='lax', secure=secure, path='/')
    response.set_cookie('access_token',  access,  max_age=ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES * 60, **common)
    response.set_cookie('refresh_token', refresh, max_age=REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS * 86400, **common)
```
NIT: Factor COOKIE_SECURE resolution into a single helper (e.g. _cookie_secure()) instead of duplicating the env read in _set_auth_cookies and auth_refresh.
critical_code_review_comments: HIGH: _set_auth_cookies (server.py:813) hardcodes secure=False; COOKIE_SECURE env is only honored in /auth/refresh. This is the main thing iteration-6 was supposed to add and it leaks on the primary auth path.

server.py is now 1683 lines — far exceeds the 700-line guideline. Time to split: /app/backend/auth.py (login/setup/refresh/logout + bcrypt + JWT + cookies), /app/backend/crypto.py (Fernet + redaction), /app/backend/scheduler.py (periodic_sync_loop), /app/backend/db_indexes.py (startup index creation).

Fernet key derivation falls back to sha256 of the passphrase if Fernet(key) raises. This is fine but undocumented — note in env.example that FERNET_KEY may be either a real urlsafe-b64 32-byte Fernet key OR a passphrase of any length (will be SHA-256-derived).
decrypt_secret() returns '' on InvalidToken — this silently masks key rotation problems. Should log a warning so operators can spot a Fernet key mismatch in production.

encrypt_secret() is idempotent (skips re-encrypt if value already starts with 'enc::v1::'). Good. But there's no migration path for plaintext-at-rest values left over from before iteration 6. Recommend a one-time migration helper or document that existing DBs need rotation.

Auto-sync loop uses await asyncio.sleep(interval) AFTER processing; if processing takes longer than interval, intervals drift. Acceptable for SSH sync. Loop correctly catches per-server and per-iteration exceptions — won't crash.

MongoDB index creation is done in startup_event without a try/except wrapper. If a duplicate constraint fails (e.g. existing dup user emails after a bad seed), the whole app will fail to start. Consider wrapping each create_index in try/except + warning log.

Audit doc inserts both 'timestamp' (ISO string) and 'ts' (BSON Date) — duplication is fine but TTL only acts on docs that have a 'ts' field. Old audit docs from prior iterations have no 'ts' so will never expire. Document or run a one-time backfill.
/api/health and /api/ready are correctly on public_router (no auth). /api/ready returns 503 on DB failure — good for k8s readiness probes.

Encryption-at-rest covers ssh.password, ssh.private_key, smtp_password. Other secrets (license file content, JWT_SECRET in .env) are not encrypted — acceptable since JWT_SECRET is at-rest only via .env file (chmod 600 by installer).

rca_of_the_issue: Bug RCA: server.py:813 `def _set_auth_cookies(response, access, refresh): common = dict(httponly=True, samesite='lax', secure=False, path='/')`. The `secure=False` is a literal, not a variable lookup. Iteration 6 added COOKIE_SECURE env handling but only patched the /auth/refresh endpoint at line 972 — the primary login + setup path which uses _set_auth_cookies was missed. Reproduction: curl -i POST /api/auth/login → Set-Cookie for access_token has only `HttpOnly; SameSite=lax`, no `Secure`. Mitigation: replace `secure=False` with `secure=os.environ.get('COOKIE_SECURE','false').lower() in ('1','true','yes')`; ideally factor into a helper used by both _set_auth_cookies and auth_refresh.
